title: Theme tokens with CSS custom properties
when: The user wants consistent colors and spacing, a theme switch, dark mode, or to recolor a whole site by changing a few values.
inputs: whether a manual theme toggle is wanted
prompt:
Goal: Every color, space, radius and font size comes from tokens on :root, and the dark theme only swaps token values.
Steps:
1. Primitives on :root: a small palette (--gray-100 to --gray-900, --brand-500), --space-1 to --space-6 on a 4 px scale, --radius.
2. Semantic tokens on top: --color-bg, --color-surface, --color-text, --color-muted, --color-accent, --color-focus; components use only these.
3. Dark values in @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) { ... } } plus :root[data-theme="dark"]; declare color-scheme: light dark.
4. Toggle: a button with aria-pressed sets document.documentElement.dataset.theme and saves the choice in localStorage inside try and catch.
5. Apply the saved theme from a tiny guarded script in head before first paint, so there is no flash.
Quality bar:
- No component hardcodes a hex value.
- Each text and background token pair reaches 4.5 to 1 in both themes.
- The focus ring stays visible on every surface.
Pitfalls:
- Pure white on pure black in dark mode, which glares; use near black surfaces.
- Unguarded storage reads that throw in private windows.
Verify:
- [ ] :root declares primitives and semantic tokens.
- [ ] A dark block exists for both the media query and data-theme.
- [ ] The toggle has a name and aria-pressed.
Output: tokens.css (or the top of style.css) with primitives, semantic tokens and the dark block; theme.js for the toggle.

examples.input: add dark mode to my site with a toggle
examples.output: semantic tokens on :root, dark overrides under prefers-color-scheme and [data-theme="dark"], toggle button saving the choice
